subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What private-session threat model and product shape should OpenClaw support for this canonical Private/Secret/Incognito mode tracker?
rationale: The requested user-visible privacy promise changes security boundaries, protocol shape, persistence behavior, plugin visibility, channels, and UI semantics; automation should not choose that contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core private session contract
options.body: Define an additive private/ephemeral session marker that every persistence, memory, plugin, channel, and UI path must enforce before exposing a user-facing toggle.

options.title: Narrow to context-only demo mode
options.body: Ship a smaller demo-mode toggle that suppresses bootstrap context but explicitly does not promise no history, no memory, or no disk persistence.

options.title: Reject core mode for now
options.body: Close or defer the feature until maintainers decide a core privacy boundary is worth the compatibility, UX, and testing cost.

recommendation.title: Design core private session contract
recommendation.body: Define an additive private/ephemeral session marker that every persistence, memory, plugin, channel, and UI path must enforce before exposing a user-facing toggle.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle authored the recent canonical-review framing and is tied by history to session, transcript, and memory surfaces that define the security boundary.
